   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

Chris Oliver To Eric Ireland

Your letter in the February
OUTLET concerning the +D to Opus
transfer utility NORAM, did not
mention if the "installed" mess-
age was displayed after loading
NORAM.

If it was, no problem with the
loading and installation is
indicated, so suggesting that
the problem lies with the drive.

Now the Opus Error Report you
obtained: "g Disc I/O error"
will occur if there is no disc
in the drive; if the information
on the disc is corrupt; or if
the disc is formatted to a
configuration different to the


drive itself (for instance if
you attempt to read an 80 track
disc in a 40 track drive).

+D discs are formatted to 80
tracks (usually), so NORAM is
ONLY usable with an 80 track
drive, and you will in fact get
the above Error Report if you
attempt to read one in a 40
track drive.

Let us know via OUTLETTERS if
you still get problems and incl-
ude as much detail as possible.

On a completely different sub-
ject: your Christmas card in the
Christmas issue of OUTLET was
excellent. We look forward to
seeing more of your work.
                         Chris

From: Keith Taylor

Dear Ron & Brian,

I didn't know whether to be
amused or humiliated to see the
two programs (Credit card and
Phone) in the last Outlet as for
the last few years I have been
running similar programs of my
own however mine have bugs (due
no doubt to bad programming)
that I haven't been able to
shift. I haven't submitted them
before out of embaressment and
also because being written in
Basic they are rather long. I
wonder if you would be interest-
ed in casting a critical eye
over them for possible future
inclusion with bugs removed of
course!

Regarding the Spectrum and its
future, I have found it perfect-
ly adequate for my needs and it
has given me many hours of equal
frustration and enjoyment. How-
ever,I think that afficionados
of Sir Clive's baby have to face
up to facts.

The older it gets and the more
technology advances, unless you
are something of a computer or
electronics buff, either fixing
or obtaining parts for it are
going to be either impossible to
get or else just not cost eff-
ective.

The 3" disc is a point in quest-
ion. Even the 3.5" discs future
is in doubt now with zip/jaz


drives and R/W discs becoming
both more common and gradually
cheaper.


Also again because of the march
of technology more and more com-
puter users will be turning to
the Web. This leaves the Speccy
out in the cold.


I for one am going to miss it
(although I hope like myself
it's demise is a while yet in
coming), because no matter how
marvellous PCs are, they will
never be as much fun as the
Speccy. From my dealings with
PCs I have reached the following
conclusions...


They are expensive monsters at
birth and grow greedier by the
year for more sophisticated and
expensive hardware.


They have a short life before
being removed from society and
placed in computerland's old
folks homes where they lie ready
to be stripped of all their
belongings and become totally
worthless.


They bestride the world like a
colossus,governing our lives at
least until year 2OOO when they
will truly get their comuppance
(fat chance).


I could go on and on but I've
just seen a couple of men in
white coats coming up the drive
and one of them seems to have
custard on his...

                   Keith Taylor





Brian Cavers to Keith Taylor

Anyone with any programs they
think might be of even the
slightest interest to others
should just send them in. It
costs no more to send a disk
than to send a letter inquiring
about it. We can then see the
program itself and decide.

The worst that can happen is
that it just doesn't get publ-
ished if not suitable, for in-
stance, if too difficult or time
consuming to correct any bugs.

                     Brian

From:Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Brian.

Thank you for passing on the
disk from George with his mods
to my routine "FINDOUT" that was
in Outlet some years ago. It is
always interesting to see how
others use routines and mods for
their own requirements. It also
helps to get ideas of how to
present programs for others to
use.

When I wrote the program I
recall disks were about `1.50 a
time. Being able to get 2 or 3
issues of Outlet on one disk was
a big saving. Out of interest I
had a look back at past issues.


I keep the original Outlet as a
master and make a "working" copy
for day to day use. So at the
time by combining issues of
Outlet on "masters" I gained
some 22 disks and the working
copies reduced by 22 so making
some 44 less disks in all. This
worked out a saving of over `60!
at that time.

Now with "reclaimed" disks at
15p - 20p I must admit I tend
not to count them these days,
rather slap happy, disks every-
where with not much on. Mind you
it does make life more difficult
to find a particular item.

               Malcolm Perry

From: J. Woodhead, WEST YORKS



Dear Ron,

Will a 24-pin printer interface
with my +3 Spectrum function as
successfully as a 9-pin printer
(serial and/or parallel)? Will a
24-pin printer give as good or
better results with...

1. Wordmaster (Typeliner)

2. Art Studio

3. The Outlet Tabloid option

        ...bearing in mind their
special print routines?


Thank you for sending back issue
No.75. I find it has the same
bug in the serial print routine
as is in No76.The cures for this
which you gave in your reply to
my letter in Outlet 120 Aug 97
both worked perfectly and also
work with Issue 75, EXCEPT the
2 files MFINFO1.# and MFINFO2.#
which still won't print with the
printer (LX400) in serial mode.
They will print in parallel mode
but in this mode the printer al-
ways double spaces not only with
Outlet files but using other
programs as well. WHY? And yes,
in desperation I have even read
the printer handbook and follow-
ed the instructions (Dip Switch
2:4 off) it doesn't make any
difference. Can you help?
                    J. Woodhead

Brian Cavers to J. Woodhead

As I understand it, 24-pin prin-
ters work just the same as 8-pin
when run by normal software - it
should just give better quality.
However, there was a slight
glitch with OUTLET text which
we cured by adding an extra
option in the print menu. If
you are reading this on-screen,
press P to initialize print (if
you have not done so already)
and you will see the bottom op-
tion shows LINESPACE 24. If you
press L repeatedly it will togg-
le between 20 and 24. This will
solve the problem. It was to do
with the slight variation in the
height of the text as I remember
and this adjusts line spacing to
fit on a page.

However,that glitch was only be-
cause we wanted to fit an exact
number of lines on a page for
our TABLOID printout. Normally
in any software it will not
matter. Printing out graphics
from such as Art Studio should
not make any differece as they
will be using the 8-pin method.
To get improved graphics you
will need 24-pin software I
think.

Can any readers who have 24-pin
printers advise on their experi-
ence with this?

                     Brian

From: Colin Bibby
I'd like to start here with a
word or two of gratitude and
thanks to a fab Outlet team. I
have thoroughly enjoyed my first
12 months with Outlet. LONG MAY
YOU REIGN!

It isn't often these days I find
such complete and down to earth
chat with so much dedication for
and from all those aboard. My
heart does throw a bit of a
wobbler however each time one or
another Outlet supporter decides
to talk of alternatives. Oh yes,
the Outlet zine may certainly go
bi-monthly, or even quarterly.
But an alternative to Outlet?
There isn't one as far as I am
aware still using original ZX
syntax.

Chezron are obviously the last
group supplying to the bona fide
fellow ZXer although not a tape
version, 3" or 3.5" only with
the addition of a +D version for
those in need. But no others
exist for the ZX syntax as far
as I am aware on either tape or
disk.

Of course, the 3" floppy disk
seems to be the main stumbling
block. Chezron Software were
quite obviously well ahead in
the game securing an excess of
3" discs while the going was
good. Since these are no longer
manufactured, well, need I say
more ? Sob... WHERE ELSE ?

THANKS FOR THE LAST 12 MONTHS.


+3 3.5" fdd hint: Omitted from
previous detail concerning the
addition of a standard 1.44Meg
drive for +3. In brief here:-

Although the 1.44 (HD) drive is
ideal for the +3 "B:" port, most
will need an additional sticker
(sellotape or similar) to close
an extra hole opposite the write
protect trapdoor. Alternatively
use DD 720K discs which have
only one such hole (the write
protect hole).

Since there's some controversy
over mixing HD/DD disks/drives,
it might be wise to stick with
the HD disk for HD drives and DD
disk for DD drives though I per-
sonally use mainly HD disks in
both with no obvious problems.

All sweet and smooth. But don't
forget that extra hole mentioned
in the HD disk which might need
blocking off with a sticker be-
fore you can even format a 3.5"
disk for your +3.

HINT. Stock up. These also will
dry up as the 2Meg and other
newer drives appear for those
less satisfied modern PC freaks.

NOW A LITTLE HELP REQUIRED. It
seems logical that the Tas 3
dictionary/spellchecker etc can
be used with Wordmaster.BUT HOW?

                  Colin Bibby

Brian Cavers to Colin Bibby

Thanks, Colin.

Tas-Spell seems to merge into
Tasword 3 on the +3 and check
the text file already loaded in
Tasword. Therefore without very
clever re-writing in machine
code I don't see how it can be
made to check a WordMaster file.
without first converting the
file from WordMaster to Tas3
format.

I thought we'd had a Tas 3 to
WordMaster convertor in OUTLET
but I can't find it now.Anyone?

                      Brian

From: J. Littlemore, FLINTSHIRE

Dear Brian,

Before I ordered my 3.5" drive
from Chris Box I purchased three
boxes of 10 3.5" DS.DD disks
hoping that I could transfer two
old Outlet disks onto one 3.5"
disk, but they will not go into
the drive on the reverse side
including the test one you sent
me I hope that there is nothing
on the other side as I can't
access it.

There was a disk with the drive
to format 3.5" to 706K and 3" to
173K. It also does a CAT on A
and B and it can copy A to B or
B to A


I have one snag with the 3.5"
drive: I have four programs from
Kobrasoft namely: SP7, a tape to
disk program; D.I.C.E V3.0, you
did an article on this not long
ago;D.M.S Disk Management System
and Diary & Database.

SP7 I am not worried about as I
have done all the transfers I
need.

DICE I would I would like to
work as it is very useful.

Diary & DATABASE I can still use
on 3" disk.

DMS I have all my disk on this
including all OUTLETS up to 125
JAN 98. All these are on file
that I can print out a listing.

The only way I can think of is
to copy half of it onto side A
of a 3" disk and the other half
onto side B. and, as the copy is
in CAT order and not contents
order, it's not a true copy. I
can then load them into DMS as
side A for both sides to be a
list of the 3.5" disk. You can't
do a full disk copy as the 3"
fills up before it's completed
even when formatted to 203K.
This also takes a long time to
do.
               Yours Sincerly,

               J. Littlemore

PS Should I send future articles
on 3.5" disks instead of 3" as I
have my Tasword on 3.5" now?

Brian Cavers to J. Littlemore





3.5" drives access BOTH sides of
a disk without you having to
turn it over. There is a little
man inside who turns it over. He
used to work in our fridge turn-
ing the light on and off but now
with advancing technology he got
promoted - and well, the rest is
history.

Seriously, there are two read/
write heads in the drive - one
for each side (and a little man
with two heads is better than
one)


From a user point of view you do
not normally need to concern
yourself about sides but just
regard the disk as one big side
(with a little man standing on
the corner out of work)

It is possible to put two +3
OUTLET disks onto a 3.5" in some
cases. However, many are too big
(say two at 380K each that comes
to 760K - too big for the 710 or
720K). The method is to use a
different user area. A second
problem is that OUTLET will only
run in User Area 0 (the default)
because on the +3 you cannot set
the current user area like you
can the drive - it is always 0.
This means that when OUTLET
tries to load the next file in
say, user area 1 it tries 0!

If you want to experiment with
user areas, they are described
on Page 146 of the +3 manual.
They are rather like a poor
man's subdirectory. Basically,
say you wanted to load a file
from User area 1 on Drive B you
would use...

LOAD "1B:FILENAME"

You cannot make 1 the 'current'
default user area and you cannot
omit the drive letter either.Bit
restrictive what?

There are 16 user areas from 0
to 15. I use area 1 on the 3.5"
version of the Plus 3 OUTLET to
store files so I can recreate
the 3" disk from a 3.5"!


Anyone who has the 3.5" version
of the Plus 3 OUTLET can see
these files by entering +3 BASIC
and entering...

CAT "1B:"

These files are the'DISK' loader
and 'CONTENTS' programs from
Side B of the 3" equivalent ver-
sion and two data files holding
the filenames for each side. If
anyone wants to know how to re-
create a 3" version from the 3.5
then let me know. I have a prog-
ram that does it automatically.
Perhaps I could put it in an
OUTLET if there is any interest?

So, it's hardly worth the hassle
of trying to cram two OUTLETs on
one 3.5". But, if you do...

Check how much room there is
left on the two 3" OUTLETs. The
disks are formatted to 203K on
each side. Subtract what is left
and calculate total space needed
and that has to fit on say,700K.

Whether you transfer one or two
3" OUTLETs to a 3.5" it is very
important to transfer Side B
first and then Side A.

The 'Turn to Side B' prompt can
be ignored - just press a key.
If it bothers you then delete
line 99 in CONTENTS. To do this
is rather messy itself!...


This is the way I recommend...



1. Reset the machine.
2. Enter 128K BASIC
3. Enter LOAD "B:"
3. Enter MERGE "CONTENTS"
4. Wait for OK to show.
5. Enter 99
6. Enter LIST 9972
7. Delete A: from "A:CONTENTS"
   in line 9972 so it is just
   "CONTENTS"
8. Enter RUN 9970

I must admit I don't really und-
erstand your statements about
DMS,etc. I think you may be ask-
how to transfer them to a 3.5"
disk and/or run them so they can
access a 3.5" disk. I assume you
mean they will not copy over by
the normal method. If they also
do not work with a 3.5" disk it
may not be easy to change them.

Let me have more details if you
want to know more. I do not have
any of these programs myself.
Does anyone else?

Send articles, etc. on either 3"
or 3.5" disks - whichever is
most convenient for you.

                        Brian

From: L.G. Baumann




A Question
----------

The symbol "&" is spoken as
"and";it is called an Ampersand.
The symbol "@" is spoken as
"at". But does it have a name?
Perhaps one of your readers can
provide an answer. I cannot find
it in any dictionary and it is
used frequently in Internet
addresses and, of course, in
POKE @ for the Plus D. I have
been told but not verified that
in German it is called "rat
tail".


A Program Bug
-------------
I have found a small error that
I made in a program I wrote and
which was included in Outlet 84
in August 1994 as "Multicopy".
The program enables a list of
files to be chosen for copying
to another disc in a desired
order, with the ability to
change the order before finally
doing the actual copying. The
bug is not serious but is annoy-
ing and readers might like to
know of it. Line...

1260 IF a$(1)="#" THEN GOTO 1110

should read...

1260 IF a$(1)="#" THEN GOTO 1260


The error only surfaces if,
after choosing files for copy-
ing, one decides to change the
order again and by mistake
specifies the same file twice.
This causes the screen display
to move up a line spoiling
everything. One can then only
mutter a few well-chosen words
of annoyance and start all over
again. My apologies to anyone
who has suffered.

                   L.G. Baumann.

Ron Cavers to L.G. Baumann

Like you, I have been unable to
find a dictionary entry for the
@ sign. A couple of the Internet
dictionaries actually use it as
a control in their search facil-
ity so it impossible to search
for the character itself!

However, dredging the innermost
reaches of my memory, I seem to
recall school text books that
used to lay-out simple arithmet-
ic problems thus:

12 toffees at 1d each =
14 beans   "  2d  "   =
etc, etc. This later became:

12 toffees @ 1d  =
14 beans   @ 2d  =

In other words, the @ replaced
not only the "at" but also the
"each" so it is an abbreviation
for "at, each". But I have no
idea whether it has a formal
name like the ampersand.

Any other offers, anyone?

                        Ron

From: Brian Cavers

I may have asked this one before
so apologies if so. If you turn
up the brightness and contrast
too high on a TV or monitor the
picture becomes slightly blurred
and out of focus. Old TVs and
monitors get dimmer and dimmer
so over the years one gradually
is turning up the brightness and
contrast. Eventually you reach
the 'zone of blurring' and have
to compromise between sufficient
brightness and sufficient sharp-
ness of picture.

Is it possible to re-focus the
cathode ray tube to give it a
few more years of life? One for
Malcolm Perry I guess!
                           Brian

From:Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

         Maths problem:
My mother said a quiz show on
the TV asked "what is a 1/4 of a
1/2?". I did the logical thing
and divided a 1/2 into 4, 1/4
segments so each part was 1/8.
So said 1/8th.

Mother said the TV had said it
was 2 but how could it be? that
must be wrong. That was when my
brain decided to start working
and I recalled the "rules of
maths" Yes, divided a fraction
by a fraction and you get a
larger number! multiply and it
is smaller. The calculator con-
firmed that 1/2 divided by 1/4
was in fact 2. so TV was right.
Or were they?

Incidentally I still have and
use the original Sinclair progr-
ammable calculator, the one with
reverse notation and you have to
do things backwards. Hand it to
an unsuspecting person and watch
their face when they realise it
does not have an '=' key! I also
bought the small calculator kit
at `30 which then reduced to `l9
ready buily then had it nicked.
All in 12 months!

Back to the plot. The question
is in fact ambiguous as by
saying "what is a 1/4 of a 1/2"
it is surely not specifying
enough detail. Looking at it
from a pure maths point of view
yes the answer is 2 but from a
practical point if you divided


anything up you never get more
than you started with so 2 is
impossible.

If you have half a cake and ask
what is a 1/4 it would be a mir-
acle and headlines in the press
if you ended up with 2 cakes!

So assuming my mother heard the
question correctly was the
correct answer "2" or should it
be the logical answer of 1/8?

           Malcolm

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

I do not wish to be divisive but
your letter is half-right and
half-wrong and all factors being
equal, your fourth paragraph is
fractionally better than its
third sentence. To sum up, if I
can just add one more part to
the equation, half a loaf is
better than none so a quarter of
that half must be worse than
some. I tend to get a bit short
with long division but long for
a short when multiplying and I
can't see the point of decimals.

                       Brian.

3.5" drives access BOTH sides of a disk without you having to turn it over. There is a little man inside who turns it over. He used to work in our fridge turn- ing the light on and off but now with advancing technology he got promoted - and well, the rest is history.

Seriously, there are two read/ write heads in the drive - one for each side (and a little man with two heads is better than one)

1. Reset the machine. 2. Enter 128K BASIC 3. Enter LOAD "B:" 3. Enter MERGE "CONTENTS" 4. Wait for OK to show. 5. Enter 99 6. Enter LIST 9972 7. Delete A: from "A:CONTENTS" in line 9972 so it is just "CONTENTS" 8. Enter RUN 9970

Brian
